 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. BOSTON — Maine native Cooper Flagg struggled with efficiency in his first matchup against the Celtics at TD Garden during his rookie season last year.
 The 19-year-old shot 30.4% from the floor (7-of-23), including 0-for-4 from 3-point range.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement He'll get a second crack at it against the team he grew up rooting for when the Mavericks and Celtics tip off at 6 p.m. Sunday.
 "There's a lot of Maine here to support him," first-year Mavericks coach Dusty May said. "So I think this part of the country, they appreciate good ball. They appreciate those from here. And so we anticipate he'll get a very, very kind ovation."
 Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla sees an improved Flagg in his second season. The 6-foot-9 forward is averaging 24.1 points, 7.0 rebounds and 6.4 assists per game through 12 games.
 "Late-game execution," Mazzulla said about Flagg's biggest area of development from his rookie season. "Does a great job getting to the spots. Does a good job getting to the free throw line. I think his competitiveness, his decision-making. He's just becoming an all-around player. So he's a guy that you have to pick your poison — what you want to live with, what you're willing to take away. Just puts a ton of pressure on all three levels, especially the free-throw line."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Mazzulla said having a young player with the ability to draw fouls and get to the line is "a difference-maker" for a team. Flagg has converted 72-of-82 free throw attempts, an 88% success rate.
 "That's one of the biggest keys when you're playing against him — is keeping him off the free-throw line," Mazzulla said.
 Based on watching film of Flagg's rookie season, May said he thinks the star is "a little bit better in every area."
 "He looks stronger," May said. "He looks just more acclimated to the NBA game. I think last year he definitely had bright moments, but it was up and down like it is for all rookies. This year, he's been pretty consistent. He's had a couple nights where it hasn't been his best, but for the most part, when you look at his body of work, he's been very, very good for us."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement May said he's "fascinated by" how Flagg has been able to handle himself as an NBA player at just 19.
 "If we all just closed our eyes and imagined ourselves at 19, it's unfathomable to be in the situation that these guys are (in)," May said. "I'm blown away at when I just watch how much these guys are able to do — back-to-backs, getting off a plane at 3 a.m. and then going out and as soon as the lights are on, they're able to do it again. And so for a 19-year-old to be able to do and manage what he's done is impressive. And also it's fun to watch him because he's still getting better."
